title: The approved Product Contract and the PRD dossier are readable on the goal
description:
SPIDR child 2 of task-e7a20a498ed0436380e5aca23cb81607 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). Dependency-free LEAF; parallel with child 1.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: two daemon reads that are SERVED but have no screen, given one each. (a) The approved Product Contract dossier on the opened goal from `/product-contract/gate-1/read`: personas/journeys, requirements, criteria WITH their coverage state, assumptions, unresolved decisions, versions. (b) The document dossier on the PRD panel from `/documents/dossier/read`.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb - both reads exist DAEMON-SIDE, so this row is browser work plus decoders, not new routes:
- `apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-read-dispatch.ts` imports `PRODUCT_CONTRACT_GATE_1_READ_PATH` with `handleProductContractGate1ReadRequest` (:11-12) and `DOCUMENT_DOSSIER_PATH` with `handleDocumentDossierReadRequest` (:3). Both are wired.
- `/documents/dossier/read` is ALREADY in the browser's proxy roster (apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts:16); `/product-contract/gate-1/read` is NOT - so that one needs its proxy pin as well as its decoder.
- `grep -rn 'gate-1/read' apps/control-room/src` returns nothing outside the proxy list, so neither read is consumed by a screen today. That is the gap, and it is real.

THE DECODER DISCIPLINE: every live read client in apps/control-room/src/live/ decodes with an EXACT-KEY record check that REFUSES a response whose key set differs, rather than silently defaulting - a stale daemon is detected, not papered over. Follow that shape (live-sessions.ts is a compact example); a decoder that tolerates extra keys is how a shape change ships unnoticed.

CRITERIA COVERAGE STATE is the load-bearing column: the contract dossier shows each criterion WITH whether it is covered, which is what makes the screen worth opening rather than a formatted dump of the contract.
definitionOfDone: The opened goal shows the approved Product Contract dossier from `/product-contract/gate-1/read`: the approved revision id, the requirements count, and every criterion WITH its coverage state. Assert against a REAL daemon frame that a named criterion's coverage state reaches the row - a dossier that lists criteria without coverage is a formatted dump, not a dossier.
The PRD panel shows the document dossier from `/documents/dossier/read`.

Both reads have an EXACT-KEY decoder that REFUSES an unexpected key set rather than defaulting, with a test for each: a real frame decodes; a frame with an extra key is refused; a frame missing a key is refused. `/product-contract/gate-1/read` also gains its proxy pin in dev-proxy-paths.ts (`/documents/dossier/read` is already there at :16 - do not duplicate it).

Every digest mirror and roster the new decoders touch is updated together: packages generated-coverage.test.ts, apps/control-room/src/data/data-adapter.test.ts and v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx are the ones the parent row names - verify each by running it, and if one does not in fact pin this surface, say so in the step note rather than editing it for symmetry.
Refusals render VERBATIM with their codes on both screens - a goal whose contract read refuses must say so, not render an empty dossier that reads as 'no requirements'.

This row adds NO daemon route: `git diff --stat` shows no file under apps/daemon/src. Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` (the packages digest mirrors are touched, so the root lane is real evidence here).
taskRails: BROWSER-ONLY. Both reads are already served; this row writes decoders and screens. A daemon change means the read is not what it claims - stop and report rather than editing it.
EXACT-KEY DECODERS, matching every sibling in apps/control-room/src/live/. A tolerant decoder defeats the mechanism that detects a stale daemon.

AN EMPTY DOSSIER IS NEVER RENDERED AS EMPTINESS. A refusal renders its code; absence of data renders words saying so. The difference matters because an operator reads an empty requirements list as 'the contract has none'.
ASCII-only sources and apostrophe-free JSX text (scheduler package-boundary scan); check any new testid namespace is free; keep every production file under 250 lines.

implementationPlan.description: THE CONTRACT DOSSIER ON THE GOAL. Render the approved revision id, the requirements count, and EVERY CRITERION WITH ITS COVERAGE STATE, plus personas/journeys, assumptions, unresolved decisions and versions. THE COVERAGE COLUMN IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE: a list of criteria without coverage is a formatted dump of the contract, and the operator can already read the contract — what they cannot see anywhere else is which criteria are actually covered. Assert against a REAL daemon frame that a NAMED criterion's coverage state reaches the rendered row, not merely that a table rendered. Keep the screen in its own module under apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/ and under 250 lines.

WHAT IT RENDERS, per cited contract: contractId, the APPROVED REVISION ID and plane; the DURABLE Gate 1 verdict from the new /product-contract/gate-1/read (approved-by-a-named-human plus the revision digest core stamped, or the refusal verbatim with code and layer); the REQUIREMENTS COUNT and the criteria count; then every requirement with EVERY CRITERION AND ITS COVERAGE STATE (data-status plus the visible status word plus the sealed nodeKey when one carries it).

WHY TWO READS AND NOT ONE - the measurement from step 1, restated because it drives the design. /product-contract/gate-1/read serves a four-key VERDICT {advisoryOnly, gate:"GATE_1", ok, revisionDigest}; it carries no requirement, criterion or coverage state. /documents/coverage/read serves exactly those, including the revision triple the gate read needs as input. So the dossier composes: coverage says WHAT the contract asks for and how far it is covered, gate-1 says WHETHER a named human approved that exact revision, derived from the stored grant rather than from the coverage join's gate1 hint. Neither is used as a stand-in for the other, and useContractGates keys each read by the JSON triple so a new revision is a new read (JSON, not a delimiter: a delimiter is a guess about what an id cannot contain).

implementationPlan.description: REFUSALS RENDER, ABSENCE IS WORDS. Both surfaces render a refusal VERBATIM with its code. And the distinction that matters: a goal whose contract read REFUSES must say so — it must NOT render an empty dossier, because an empty requirements list reads to an operator as 'this contract has no requirements', which is a different and false claim. Assert three states per surface: a real frame renders; a refusal renders its code; genuinely-absent data renders words saying it is absent. Also assert that a refusal on ONE of the two reads does not blank the OTHER.
implementationPlan.note:
REFUSALS RENDER, ABSENCE IS WORDS, AND THE TWO READS ON EACH SURFACE ARE INDEPENDENT.

CONTRACT DOSSIER - five new arms in contract-dossier.test.tsx, each asserting the POSITIVE words AND the negative that makes them load-bearing:
(1) COVERAGE REFUSAL: `DOCUMENT_COVERAGE_READ_GOAL_UNBOUND @ DOCUMENT_COVERAGE_READ` renders verbatim, and cr.contract.body, cr.contract.none and the criterion row are ALL absent. That last triple is the point of the arm - a card that swallowed the refusal and rendered an empty dossier would still pass an assertion that only checked the refusal text.
(2) GATE 1 REFUSAL: `APPROVAL_HUMAN_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED @ HUMAN_AUTHORITY_GATE` renders verbatim, the approved-verdict line is ABSENT, and INDEPENDENCE holds - crit-sso-1 still renders data-status VERIFIED and the requirements count still reads "1 requirements". One read refusing does not blank the other.
(3) GENUINE ABSENCE IN WORDS, at two depths, both produced by running an emptied WIRE frame through the production decoder (not typed straight in): zero contracts renders "No Product Contract cites this PRD yet." with NO refusal note; a requirement carrying zero criteria renders "This requirement carries no acceptance criterion yet."
(4) BEFORE THE FIRST ANSWER: "Reading the contract..." with no body and no absence claim - not-yet-read and genuinely-empty are different sentences.
(5) A THROWN coverage read becomes a VISIBLE `CONTRACT_DOSSIER_COVERAGE_READ_FAILED @ CONTROL_ROOM_GOALS` with no body, so a network failure can never present as "this contract asks for nothing".

PRD PANEL - two new arms plus the two already landed in step 4 (real frame renders; DOCUMENT_WORK_DOSSIER_MISSING @ DAEMON_READ_MODEL renders verbatim with no body). The new pair proves INDEPENDENCE in BOTH directions on the panel: with the dossier read refusing, cr.prd.text still shows the stored PRD bytes; with /goals/source/read refusing GOAL_SOURCE_UNBOUND ("This goal was created without a PRD."), the dossier still renders every source binding. To make that assertable, LivePrd gained one optional injectable prop, `dossierTransport`, mirroring its existing `read` prop; production passes nothing and keeps the default fetch path.
